page.overview:
Who is Chris Bristow?

Chris Bristow (born December 2 1937 in Lambeth, London, UK - died June 19 in Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps, Belgium) was a Formula One racing driver. He was killed during the 1960 Belgian Grand Prix, only minutes within the death of Alan Stacey.

Early in his career, he earned the nickname "the wild man of British club racing". He had spun or been in a collision nearly every race that he had participated in.

Bristow's Formula One career began after he was invited to racing in the 1959 British Grand Prix as a third driver for the British Racing Partnership. He managed to place his Formula Two car in 10th, but was not invited back for the rest of the season.

Bristow returned to Formula One in the season, racing in the Monaco Grand Prix, Dutch Grand Prix and Belgian Grand Prix with the Yeoman Credit Racing team.
